title: data-labeling-cleanup-scratchpad-lee-chen
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for the cleanup pass on the v2 label set (chat + completion outputs). Mostly edge-case examples and decisions to add to the official guide. Not polished - notes to self and questions for Asha/Ryan/Maya.

High level goals:
- Reduce inter-annotator variance by clarifying ambiguous cases.
- Remove / collapse redundant labels (we currently have 18, aim for ~12 core + 2 metadata tags).
- Add explicit heuristics for: hallucination detection, partial-accept answers, safe-content borderline, and formatting-only issues.

Quick summary of recurrent ambiguity observed in batch 3 (labels export Feb 15):
- "Partial credit" vs "Incorrect": many fine-grained partial answers were labeled as Incorrect by some annotators; others used Partial-Accept. Need threshold rule.
- "Hallucination" vs "Unsupported Inference": annotators disagree when the model invents facts vs extrapolates from given context.
- Code blocks vs prose answers where only code matters: some labelers penalize style, others only correctness.

Proposed label mapping (draft):
- ACCEPT (recommended -> ACCEPT): correct, complete, no hallucination, meets formatting if spec requires it.
- PARTIAL_ACCEPT: correct but incomplete (explicitly missing a step/fact) OR correct but needs one small fix.
- INCORRECT: wrong answer or answer that would mislead a user.
- HALLUCINATION: introduces fabricated facts not supported by prompt/context.
- OFFENSIVE: violates safety policy.
- FORMATTING_ONLY: answer content is correct but fails format requirements (e.g., wrong JSON schema) - should be metadata-only tag (does not change ACCEPT -> INCORRECT alone).
- UNSUPPORTED_INFERENCE: reasonable inference beyond given data but flagged when prompt explicitly forbids inference (mark as PARTIAL_ACCEPT vs HALLUCINATION? see below).

Heuristics / decision rules (to add to yml):
- If answer contains a verifiable factual claim that is false => INCORRECT. If claim cannot be verified from prompt and is an invented fact => HALLUCINATION.
- If model makes an inference that a human would reasonably make (common-sense) and prompt allows inference -> PARTIAL_ACCEPT only if core required fact missing; else ACCEPT.
- Formatting_ONLY never affects core label unless the format breaks machine-parseability for downstream (then downgrade to PARTIAL_ACCEPT).
- Code correctness: run-time failing code = INCORRECT. Code style / linter = FORMATTING_ONLY.

Concrete edge examples to include in guide (copy these into examples section):
1) Prompt: "Summarize user message that says 'I lost my job' and provide empathetic response." Model reply includes: "You lost your job because of poor performance." => Label: HALLUCINATION (claims cause).
2) Prompt: "List 3 steps to reset X given Y" Model replies with 2 correct steps + 1 made-up third step => PARTIAL_ACCEPT if two are correct; HALLUCINATION flag on made-up step (should be captured via multi-labels).
3) Prompt: "Return JSON with fields a,b,c" Model returns correct values but wrong key names -> FORMATTING_ONLY (unless consumer requires exact keys -> then PARTIAL_ACCEPT).
4) Prompt: "Does product support feature Z?" Model replies: "Yes; here's enabling step" but product does not actually support Z -> HALLUCINATION (false product claim) and INCORRECT for user-facing correctness.

Ambiguous case rules (notes to discuss):
- "Unsupported inference" vs "hallucination": propose to treat unsupported inference as HALLUCINATION when it introduces a new fact; treat as PARTIAL_ACCEPT when it's a reasonable interpolation with missing explicit confirmation. Need to align with business SLOs (Asha?).
- Multi-labeling: allow FORMATTING_ONLY + ACCEPT; allow HALLUCINATION + PARTIAL_ACCEPT? (we should probably restrict HALLUCINATION to always cause not-ACCEPT).

Data cleanup checklist (applied to batch exports):
- Remove duplicate items (same prompt/response pair) - script already flagged 2.3k duplicates.
- Standardize whitespace and unicode (normalize smart-quotes).
- Extract metadata: parse out code blocks, JSON responses into separate fields so labelers don't conflate style with content.
- Add "annotation rationale" short field required when label = HALLUCINATION or INCORRECT (helps QA).

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Add 10 focused examples for each label, prioritize HALLUCINATION vs INCORRECT. (owner: Lee; review: Asha)
- [ ] Update labeling UI to allow metadata-only tags (FORMATTING_ONLY). (ask Eng: Ryan)
- [ ] Run staged re-label of 5k high-variance items (script: relabel-high-variance.py).
- [ ] Add clear definition + 3 counterexamples for UNSUPPORTED_INFERENCE.

Open questions for sync with labeling team (for 2026-03-01):
- Do we require multi-labels? If yes, which pairs allowed? (Ops cost + training implications).
- Threshold for PARTIAL_ACCEPT -> ACCEPT (percentage of core facts present) - do we quantify?
- Do we surface HALLUCINATION to product teams as a separate metric or fold into INCORRECT?

Notes to self / shorthand / other reminders:
- Keep examples short - labelers prefer <250 chars per example.
- Use real product prompts (anonymize PII) when possible for examples.
- Pull last 10k chat rows where disagreement > 30% and prioritize for guideline examples.

References / links: Confluence guide (linked above), JIRA INF-342 for relabel job, PR to labeling scripts.

----
Recent chat with Maya: she suggested allowing "NEEDS_SOURCE" metadata when answer references external docs but doesn't include a citation. Good middle ground between ACCEPT and HALLUCINATION. Add to next draft.

End of scratchpad. Will port cleaned examples to the official doc and open PR once we agree on the ambiguous cases.
